messages:
customer@acme: Hey team — live customers seeing websocket stream stall after ~30s, then all buffered chunks arrive at once. Happens on our Private deployment inside VPC.
anya (support): Thanks for reporting — can you confirm this only happens over your Private/VPC endpoint and not hosted API?
customer@acme: Correct, hosted works fine. Private endpoints (VPC peering) intermittently stall, manifests as silence on client for 20-40s then a big flush.
sam (eng-runtime): Likely a middlebox/proxy buffering issue. Do you have any fronting proxies/load-balancers or corporate appliances on the egress path?
jordan (netops): Any TLS termination in the middle? SNI rewriting? Our obs in similar cases showed TCP idle timeouts & TLS record coalescing.
customer@acme: Traffic goes through our NG-Proxy (corporate) then to our firewall -> NAT gateway -> Redwood Private endpoint. No TLS termination (pass-through).
anya (support): Can you reproduce with a simple wscat client to narrow layer? Also share the exact sequence length/time when it stalls if possible.
customer@acme: Repro steps I used:

```
# from inside customer subnet
wscat -c "wss://private.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=rxdemo" 
# send prompt, then watch for streaming chunks
```

It prints tokens for ~10s then nothing for ~35s then a flood of tokens.

sam (eng-runtime): Can you run a tcpdump on the client side during the stall and post a small pcap? We're looking to see if TCP keepalive, PSH flags, or TLS records are being held.
jordan (netops): Also run `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.example:443 -tls1_2 -msg` and `-tls1_3` to compare record behaviours. If middlebox is coalescing TLS records it can buffer application data until idle timeout.
customer@acme: Attaching a trimmed tcpdump (sent separately). Quick note: when we tail the client socket there were small TLS records inbound during the stall but nothing delivered to app.
anya (support): That points to a middlebox doing TCP-level buffering or socket reassembly before passing up. Does your NG-Proxy implement HTTP/2 or do any connection pooling?
customer@acme: NG-Proxy is an L7 terminator for other services but we set it to TCP pass-through for this route. It still has a connection manager and an idle timeout of 30s.
sam (eng-runtime): If the proxy's idle timeout is 30s that matches the behavior. Proxies sometimes buffer until they decide the downstream connection is idle and then flush. Two quick mitigations: enable websocket pings/keepalive at the client every 10s, or change proxy config to disable request buffering / set lower buffering thresholds and increase idle timeout.
jordan (netops): Another option is to set TCP keepalive or smaller TLS record sizes on the server side; we can toggle `ws_opts.write_chunk_size` to emit smaller frames more frequently. But changing middleware is ideal.
customer@acme: We don't control the NG-Proxy config much. Can Redwood send server-side keepalives or do anything on the Private endpoint?
sam (eng-runtime): On the Private runtime we can enable periodic websocket pings from the server side per-tenant as a short-lived workaround. We can also emit explicit application-level progress events (no-ops) every 10s. I can flip that for your tenant for testing.
anya (support): For longer-term, recommend coordinating with netops to: 1) increase proxy idle timeout to > 90s for passthrough routes, 2) disable any "buffer responses until complete" features, and 3) allow TLS record streaming (no re-chunking).
jordan (netops): Also double-check firewall/egress allowlist for any intermediate appliance doing deep packet inspection (DPI) — those often pause flows while inspecting.
customer@acme: We'll try to ask NG-Proxy team to adjust idle timeout. Meanwhile would appreciate Redwood enabling server-side pings for our tenant.
sam (eng-runtime): I'll enable server-side pings for your tenant and drop a note when done. Also please share the pcap link here once results are in.
anya (support): Creating support ticket and escalation to eng-runtime. Assigned to sam. ETA for change: ~1 business day.
infra-bot: Deployment: feature/tenant-ws-ping -> canary scheduled on private-runtime-3 at 1857001300.
sam (eng-runtime): Canary complete, pings enabled for tenant acme-org. Please repro and paste client logs.
customer@acme: Re-tested. Client receives small keepalive frames and the streaming no longer stalls — continuous tokens now. Looks resolved with server pings.
anya (support): Great, keeping this open while you coordinate proxy change. If proxy idle set > 90s or disable buffering, can remove server pings later.
customer@acme: We'll push a request to NG-Proxy and follow up. Thanks for quick turnaround :raised_hands:
anya (support): Marking as actionable; will update ticket when proxy change confirmed.
notes: thread about websocket stall caused by customer-side proxy idle timeout; repro via wscat + tcpdump; workaround: server-side websocket pings enabled; next steps: customer to change proxy idle timeout and disable buffering
